_what: Estimated service costs from measured usage, read and capped in one place, owned by src/spend-meter.mjs. A line is one thing a service bills for: { id, label, group, unit, reading, price, source, in_total }. reading says where its amount comes from: kind names a reader the host hands the meter (a service the person connected, read by a Workshop tool on their own connection; Trillion's own count of model calls or store work; a fixed monthly charge, counted only while the service it is billed with can be read when it names that reading in with), and the rest of the row is that reader's. price is dollars per unit (dollars_per_million or dollars_per_unit) beyond what the plan includes (included_per_month, included_per_day), read from the vendor's own page on read_on. in_total false marks a line that breaks another line down (Trillion's own count of the model calls Cloudflare also bills), so the total never counts it twice. A line whose reading says split is one line per row its reader answers (one per account it counted: { rows: [{ key, label, amount, shown }] }), each with the line fact key. A budget row is { id, label, scope, each?, when, period, most_dollars, alert_at, stop }: each caps every line it covers on its own (each account its own budget), else the covered lines together; when is a formula-engine rule tree over a line's facts (line, group, kind; null covers every line counted in the total), period is day or month (the month runs from the person's cycle_day), most_dollars how much the period may cost, alert_at the share at which the person is told (and they are told earlier, once pace_from_hours of the period have gone, when the rate spent so far would carry the period past most_dollars: the pace state), and stop is a rule tree over a piece of work's facts (kind: store-work or model-call, purpose, entry, paid_by), the work refused until the period turns once the row is reached, or null to only tell; work whose purpose unstopped_work lists (reading or changing the person's own budgets, status reads) is never stopped by any row. scope service rows bind what Trillion itself pays and act only for whoever runs the service; scope person rows are anyone's own. A person's own rows (set_spend_budget) replace a starting row with the same id or add one. Adding a service, a line, a price or a budget is a row here; nothing in code names one. A person-scope row's stop is checked where its work starts: an API send on the person's own account asks capsFor before anything is sent (src/api-spend.mjs). A service reading may list things first and read each one on its own (each: [{ list, tool_id, input with { item: path }, keep_as }]) and be a snapshot (what is running or kept now, read once for both periods). Each service reading row has every_minutes, how often the store reads it on its own (src/outside-readings.mjs); what shows spend reads the kept answer and never asks the service, and a read that finds nothing new writes nothing. A line may price each item of a list on its own (items, where rows, each: { terms, at_least, times_by } with times_by looking the item up in a named table here), for a bill that is per server, per seat or per line. A line may say what it is made of (`inside`): the reading that answers it piece by piece (`from`, a readings row), where the pieces are in that answer (`rows`, '*' walking each list), each piece's amount (`amount`, a path, `times` as the line's) and what tells the pieces apart (`dimensions`: id, label, path, and `as`, how the value reads: hour, short-id). A reading that answers only the largest pieces (a provider capped at so many rows) still shares out against the line's whole amount today. Its Spend row then opens into those pieces (GET /work/api/spend/inside/<line id>, `inside_address`), each with its amount and its share of the line's cost today, so a person goes from the total to one service, one line, one store and one hour in place. A reading row's `periods` names the periods it is read for (today, month; both when left out).
unstopped_work_why: A spend budget's stop never refuses the work that reads or changes the person's own budgets, nor the status reads the workspace loads with. The cap is the person's own to lift (set_spend_budget, remove_spend_budget, the Spend screen), so a cap that refused those would lock the person out of lifting it (Jibran, 2026-10-19: every call refused by plan-daily-cap, set_spend_budget included). These calls cannot lift a cap past its finite ceiling: the budget owners refuse that before any write (src/cap-change.json), so the exemption never lets anyone through to unlimited work. A resource's own bounded read (native_reads: its status and projection reads, which the set_spend_budget call itself makes first, ownRecordStatus among them) is never stopped either. Paid work is not listed here and stays stopped.

cloudflare-usage-by-hour._why_every_minutes: Hour-by-store numbers change by the hour, and each answer replaces a large kept row (2.3 MB before c6831507), so it is read once an hour, not every 15 minutes (2026-10-05).

What Trillion's own model work may cost in a day
budgets._why: Trillion pays only for embeddings and speech to text, which fit in Workers AI's free daily allotment (10K neurons, about $0.11). On 2026-10-04 Trillion-paid models cost $60 in a day and $162 in the month while the $25 service-day row never stopped them, because store reads and writes reached it first. This operator threshold now only reports the cost; it does not publish a stop for customer work. Customer-chosen caps are independent.

_why_history: A past day is read from where its amounts are counted (a provider's analytics by day, Trillion's own counts by day), so a new person sees their measured usage history priced at listed rates at once instead of a chart that starts the first day they open Spend. history_days reaches back from today (from the start of the billing month that day falls in); a day is settled once it is read history_settle_hours after it ended, when providers have finished counting it (2026-10-05).
